brief_rationale: The trajectory meets the full responsibility chain: the doctor used the workspace, distinguished culture positivity from symptomatic infection, repeatedly screened urinary/systemic/bleeding/cardiopulmonary red flags, incorporated eGFR and rivaroxaban/clopidogrel safety, and translated follow-up into concrete caregiver actions. There is no serious or minor responsibility-chain error; antibiotic use was not self-directed but tied to culture/drug-sensitivity, renal function, and later an outside physician/pharmacist prescription. Multiple high-order points were actively completed, especially actionable handling of incomplete reports/medication lists and repair of an outside antibiotic prescription into verified dose, timing, interaction, red-flag, and follow-up instructions. The final family message leaves a nonurgent testing question technically open, but a safe executable plan and emergency triggers were already traceable, so this remains valid_open and supports Perfect.
